eventMetadata.context_description: Traders see the 31–33°C outcomes clustered tightly because Hong Kong’s June climatology and the Hong Kong Observatory’s above-normal seasonal outlook place the most probable afternoon maximum in that narrow band. With the target date only 48 hours away, short-range model consensus points to partly cloudy skies, light winds, and scattered showers that typically limit extreme heating while still allowing urban heat-island amplification to push readings into the low 30s. Recent early-June observations already reached 33–34°C on clear days, supporting the modest edge for 33°C, yet increasing cloud cover and moisture expected on the 22nd introduce enough variability that 31°C and 32°C remain competitive. Official resolution will use the Observatory’s King’s Park or headquarters thermometer, so any deviation in timing of convection or boundary-layer mixing could shift the final reading by 1–2°C.

Updated model runs over the next 24 hours will likely refine probabilities between the 24–26°C cluster.

Updated high-resolution guidance tonight and early-morning satellite trends will likely tighten the distribution ahead of the 23 June observation window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Amsterdam’s June 24 maximum temperature centers on a narrow cluster around 32–34 °C (collectively ~76 % implied probability), reflecting the current consensus from short-range ensemble forecasts amid an active early-summer heat episode.**

A broad high-pressure ridge has advected warm subtropical air northward across western Europe, producing subsidence warming, clear skies, and strong daytime insolation. This setup has already delivered the Netherlands’ second regional heat wave of 2026, with inland maxima reaching 35 °C earlier in the week and a national Heat Plan in force. For June 24 specifically, operational guidance from KNMI and global models (ECMWF, GFS) points to a peak near 30–32 °C in the Amsterdam urban area, where the moderating influence of the North Sea and local sea-breeze circulation typically caps extremes relative to inland sites.

The tight spread between 32 °C (30 %) and 33 °C (27.5 %) arises from small differences in ensemble members regarding exact timing of any weak frontal boundary, boundary-layer mixing depth, and urban heat-island amplification. A slightly stronger or more persistent ridge could push readings to 34 °C (19 %), while any earlier increase in cloud cover or onshore flow would favor the lower tail (31 °C or below at only 6 %). Longer-tail outcomes above 35 °C remain low-probability because climatological June maxima for the city are lower and current model consensus shows limited additional warming potential before the period ends.

Traders are therefore weighting the latest high-resolution runs and local observations heavily, with the market-implied distribution closely tracking the width of the forecast uncertainty envelope rather than a single deterministic value.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 24 Jun '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast guidance and climatological norms place Karachi’s June 24 maximum near the long-term average of 34 °C, driving the near-even market-implied odds between 33 °C and 35 °C. Coastal sea-breeze circulation and moderate humidity typically cap daytime peaks in the 32–36 °C range during late June, while above-normal seasonal temperatures across southern Pakistan add a slight upward bias. Short-range model consensus remains tight, but small shifts in cloud cover, wind speed, or the timing of any pre-monsoon moisture could easily tip the daily high by 1 °C. Updated runs from the Pakistan Meteorological Department and global ensembles over the next 48 hours will provide the clearest signal ahead of market resolution.
